conviction_note: Nothing unpriced: the Q3 carry from NRE I's end-September BROEN exit and the fee step-up from the Q2 raise are company-disclosed and already in all three sponsored previews (Inderes, Nordea, SEB). What is left is a small negative tilt on fundraising commentary (no second or final closes announced in Q3, a hard real-estate market), so p_up sits at 49 on a 4.5% scale. The findings sum (-0.4) and the scaled number (-0.09) agree in sign; the sum is larger because each finding carries its own size while p_up stays near 50 on public evidence.

Fundraising commentary on NRE IV, Infra III, CAERUS and Natural Capital, plus visibility on Infra I or Buyout XI entering carry. This is where the move lives. Slight negative tilt for real estate, unknown for the rest

findings.finding: NRE I's final exit (its 65% of BROEN, Esbjerg, sold end-September 2026 to AGAT Ejendomme) falls in Q3, and the fund is in carry, so Q3 books carried interest. Analysts already model 1.0 MEUR (Inderes) to 1.8 MEUR (Nordea), so only an outcome above the high end would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Carry has been immaterial recently (0.3 MEUR in H1 2026). Inderes said of the October announcement that it 'contained no material new information on CapMan's earnings outlook'
findings.original_quote: Rahaston 65 prosentin omistusosuus viimeisestä sijoituskohteesta, BROEN-kauppakeskuksesta Esbjergissä, Tanskassa, myytiin syyskuun 2026 lopussa kiinteistöyhtiö AGAT Ejendommelle. Rahasto on voitonjaon piirissä, ja irtautuminen BROEN-kauppakeskuksesta tuottaa siten voitonjako-osuustuottoja. [The fund's 65% stake in its last investment, the BROEN shopping centre in Esbjerg, Denmark, was sold at the end of September 2026 to the property company AGAT Ejendomme. The fund is in carry, so the exit generates carried interest.]
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. Both Nordea (1.8 MEUR, NRE I named) and Inderes (1.0 MEUR) model it, and Inderes wrote it was already in forecasts. Only the size relative to that 1.0-1.8 range is open, and nothing public sizes it.
findings.independence: https://www.borsvarlden.com/finwire/CRF00F665C (Nordea models NRE I carry in Q3)

findings.finding: The company said the roughly EUR 500m raised in H1 (EUR 440m of it in Q2) adds more than EUR 5m of annual fee income from Q3 onwards, which is about EUR 1.25m a quarter. This sits inside the company's own statement and the analysts' fee estimates (Nordea fee income 17.1 MEUR, +12% y/y).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee profit is the line this stock trades on. Q2 2026, where Nordea called fee income and profit 'softer than expected': about -3.0% in the baseline history. Q1 2026, a strong quarter with accelerating fee profit growth: about +6.2%
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The company stated it, and both previews build the fee step-up in. A residual miss or beat on cost (summer seasonality, CAERUS/Infra debt costs) is unknowable from public sources.
findings.independence: https://www.borsvarlden.com/finwire/CRF00F79F9 (SEB expects 'a bounce back in the fee margin on new AUM raised in Q2')

findings.finding: No second or final close for any flagship fund (NRE IV, Infra III, CAERUS) was announced from July to October 2026; the release feed shows only deployments and exits. Inderes flags NRE IV fundraising as a 'significant risk' that may show up in company comments. The Finnish real-estate fund backdrop stays hard: peer eQ still has a queue of redemptions it has postponed. So the fundraising commentary, the line this stock is told to trade on, leans soft for real estate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June 2026 first closes were followed by a record-intake Q2 report, which still fell about 3% on softer fees. Inderes and Nordea both treat fundraising as 'make-or-break' for 2026. No clean prior reaction to fundraising commentary alone
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The analyst covering it wrote the risk into the public preview, and the stock is flat to slightly up into the print (+1.3% over 20 days, -3.6% over 60 days). The only unpriced part is whether management confirms it. If it were fully priced, a sell-off into the print would be visible, and there is none.
findings.independence: https://www.inderes.fi/analyst-comments/eq-lykkaa-jalleen-odotetusti-kiinteistorahastojen-lunastuksia (eQ keeps postponing real-estate fund redemptions, a Finnish sector proxy only)

findings.finding: H1 management expected exits to generate carried interest in H2, which Inderes reads as Infra I or Buyout XI entering carry. Yet no Infra I or Buyout XI exit was announced in Q3 or October; the only Q3 exits were the NRE I BROEN sale and a Growth Equity 2017 exit (Aste). Any large carry is therefore Q4 at the earliest, and the Q3 call's visibility comments are the swing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large carry quarters have moved the stock up in the past. Recent carry has been immaterial. No measured reaction to carry-visibility comments
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Inderes models only 1.0 MEUR of Q3 carry and says the visibility comments are of interest. An inference from absence in the release feed is weak, so this is sized small with a wide range. Firm Q4 carry guidance on the call would be a positive surprise.
findings.independence: https://mfn.se/cis/a/capman (release list: no Infra I or Buyout XI exit announced Jul-Oct 2026). Aste exit: https://news.cision.com/fi/capman-oyj/r/capman-growth-luopuu-omistuksestaan-markkinointipalveluyhtio-asteessa,c4369807

findings.finding: On 30 October CapMan signed a EUR 30m sustainability-linked loan (3 years, plus 2 optional) to refinance the EUR 40m bond maturing in April 2027. This removes refinancing risk early. It is not distress: it buys term-out, with an equity ratio of 58.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. The stock reacted about flat to the release
findings.why_not_priced: Public for four sessions and largely priced. Its only remaining relevance is that the Q3 report's balance-sheet commentary is de-risked.

baseline_tension: Neutral. The lean is about zero (-0.06), the run-up is small (+1.3% over 20 days, +2.1% over 5 days), the short register cannot be read below the truncation floor, and my findings net to a slight negative that does not cut against any of it.
language_note: The Finnish NRE I release (Cision, 12.10.2026) states the BROEN sale date ('myytiin syyskuun 2026 lopussa', sold at the end of September 2026) and the buyer, which puts the carry in Q3. The English Inderes comment said only 'will generate carried interest' with no timing. The quarter attribution came from the Finnish primary text
Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: every CapMan stock exchange release goes out in both languages at once, and the Inderes preview is published in English translation
lessons_applied: Reported-quarter findings that sit inside what the company and analysts already published went 4 of 14 on sign, so the carry finding was cut from +0.2 to +0.1 and the fee step-up finding from +0.2 to +0.1

'You were right about the number and too small about the move': the numbers are not pre-released (base about 7%), the history median of 2.87 is a lower bound and turnover is thin ($232k a day), so abs_move_pct was raised from 4.0 to 4.5. It is held below 7 because realised volatility is about 1% a day and no guidance event is likely (the outlook is qualitative)
Truncated-zero short register: stated in positioning_check as no anchor, not as evidence that nobody is short
Financing is a question: the loan buys a term-out of the 2027 bond, so it is signed slightly positive, not read as distress
